what: A prompt experiment on the title-block reading (scripts/eval-title-block-vlm.py, workflow title-block-vlm-evaluation): hold-out 1 (27 human-checked drawings) is dev, hold-out 2 (34) test. Variant 'label' asks for each cell's printed label with its value and how to tell O/0 and I/1; the grounded arms keep a value only when its visible_text holds a label word and the value.
rule: Pre-registered in a634803 before the calls: on dev the (variant, arm) with the highest correct - 2 x (wrong + read where no cell) is chosen, ties to fewer wrong values; test is read once with it; if the baseline wins on dev, test is not read.
findings: The baseline wins on dev (page reading, merit 17); by the rule hold-out 2 was not read and the 2026-10-25 prompts stay.

The label-citing variant read fewer values right (page 24 against 35) and transcribed worse: PKQT-03 for PKQ1-03, LIJT04.20, ZL'05, a scale of '11' for 1:1, LJTU5.34. Asking for the label beside the value did not make the copy more careful.

The same baseline prompts on the same 27 pages scored differently on two days: crop reading merit 25 on 2026-10-25 and 14 on 2026-10-27 (page 16 and 17). The spread of one prompt between runs is larger than the gap between the two prompts, so one run per variant cannot rank prompts here; a comparison would need repeats.
Grounding on cited labels removed values but kept too few right ones: the best grounded arm scored 6.
